name: Records copy the code
problem: The records repeat what the code already says: which alternatives of a solution exist, the file each lives in, and an interface's signature. Each repeated fact is kept in step by hand, or by a check that only reports the drift, so adding an alternative means editing the code and several records, and the two drift apart.
who_has_it: Developers and AI agents who add or change an alternative, and the reviewers who trust the records to describe the code.
why_it_matters: A second copy held in step by a check is upkeep, not structure. It is skipped under deadline, and a record that disagrees with the code misleads more than a missing one.
why_hard: Most of a record is intent only a person can write (the problem, the ideal, the metric), so the records cannot simply be generated from the code. Only what the code already states may be derived, and a person's text has to survive every sync.
existing_attempts: Documentation generators and schema tools derive pages from code; plugin registries and dependency-injection decorators declare alternatives in code; they do not keep intent records (problems, ideals, metrics) in step with what they derive.
